sections.content: The *pluscuamperfecto* goes one step further back: it describes something that had already happened before another moment in the past. It is formed with the *imperfecto* of *haber* plus a past participle.

items.spanish: Cuando llegamos a la estación, el tren ya había salido.
items.english: When we got to the station, the train had already left.

items.spanish: Descubrí que alguien había dejado la puerta abierta.
items.english: I discovered that someone had left the door open.

items.spanish: Nunca había visto una tormenta así.
items.english: I had never seen a storm like that.

items.spanish: Todavía no habíamos cenado cuando llegaron.
items.english: We hadn't had dinner yet when they arrived.

sections.content: *Ya*, *todavía no*, *nunca* and *antes de* often signal the *pluscuamperfecto*. Nothing goes between *había* and the participle: *ya había salido*, not *había ya salido*. Object pronouns go before *había*: *lo había visto*.
